pill.desc: white to off-white lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: Its DM1 component is 93% bound to human plasma proteins in vitro, and the liver is the primary organ for eliminating it.
clues.substance: A recombinant protein made in Chinese hamster ovary cells, carrying an average of 3.5 DM1 molecules, supplied as a sterile, preservative-free lyophilized powder.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA as single-dose vials of 100 mg or 160 mg, given as an infusion every 3 weeks.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, cardiac toxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; no contraindications. Fatigue and nausea are among the most common adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Biomarker-selected metastatic breast cancer after a prior antibody and a taxane, and adjuvant treatment of early breast cancer with residual invasive disease.
clues.mechanism: Targets HER2, and after internalization releases DM1, which binds tubulin and disrupts microtubule networks, arresting the cell cycle.

tell: A HER2-directed conjugate delivering DM1, a maytansine derivative, under a boxed warning for liver and heart toxicity.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: the elimination half-life (t 1/2 ) was approximately 4 days
